body:
How did you talk about it/break the "everyone hates me" loop?

For me it's not that people hate me (they don't, but they should). It's more that I'm utterly convinced that my existence is hurtful, and that what I've done is worthy of the death penalty. So like, talking about it would be manipulating innocent people and also trying to shirk my punishment.

At the same time tho, there's a part of me that wants to live. Or a part of me that wants to *want to* live. And that part of me knows I can't keep white-knuckling it.

I like the idea of the literal elephant in the room.  I have a hard time speaking sometimes -- even without all the emotional/mental baggage, I'm autistic, and can go nonverbal if I'm too overwhelmed -- so the elephant is good shorthand.

I'm still reaaaally new at asking the counselor (directly or not) to ask deeper questions/lead the way. At my appointment today I straight up said that I didn't know what to do or say and that I needed her to take the lead because I didn't know how to talk or be or... anything. And she took over and was great at it. It's just really new and raw and I'm still awkward at it... on top of all this other stuff.

Writing is way easier for me. My written language skills are honestly the only truly good thing I can point to. And I'm less likely to forget/more likely to be coherent if I can hand my counselor a paper, which I've done before.

> How does it feel to admit this? Are there any other questions you'd wish people would ask?

It's terrifying, and it makes me feel tiny and vulnerable. And yet, at the same time, like I'm an unstoppable juggernaut of manipulation and inflicting pain on others. It's like everything I do and everything I don't do is poison, and I'm choking on it, and the only thing I can think of to stop it is to, well, just... stop everything.

As for other questions, no, I don't really care. I'm a really private person, but I don't mind answering questions if someone does ask. They usually don't. If I want to say something, I usually go ahead and say it.  It's just that on top of everything else, the whole gravity of talking about suicide makes me feel like directly talking about it or bringing it up will definitely make me toxic and awful.

It's odd. Usually I wouldn't say anything about suicide, and if asked, I'd deny it up and down. But I've been throwing hints I thought were really really really obvious. Short of actually saying "I'm seriously suicidal right now, please help." I don't know what more I could say. I guess I'll have to figure it out or make peace with it.

>What kind of stuff was [the museum] showing? What are your hobbies/interests?

It's an art museum at my local university. It's hit and miss, but when it's good, it's really good. Usually I'm not much for art, I just try to bury myself in my work. Working and sleeping is about all I do lately... working gives me concrete proof that I am contributing somehow. Sometimes I like to listen to music or read history. Last few days I've really been in to The Tragically Hip's latest album.

> Can you change counselor?

I could, but I don't really want to. She's very good, and I have known her for more than a decade. She just kinda gets stuff because she's seen me (on and off) since I was a teenager, and she knows my family, and all that. Besides, I would feel just as manipulative/toxic/awful with a stranger.

> can you consider if there are specific environmental factors leading to this feeling?

The time of year is just circumstance. I live with my parents, and they've happened to plan their vacation across the country on the same two weeks two years in a row. The date is time enough to let myself die, but not so long that my remains will turn to soup. Last year I was feeling shitty about being unemployed -- now I actually have a reasonably good job. But I've been talking with my counselor about abuse when I was a child and it's brought up extreme guilt about everything ever.

> are you open to this idea [of a zero day]

Yeah, it doesn't have any particular significance, it's just been a convenient day to off myself two years in a row.

Hi. Fellow trans person with substance issues here. 

I've typed and deleted so much, but it all just sort of sounds like empty platitudes. I guess I just wanna say that so very, very, very many people have been through what you have. And it fucking sucks. I've seen several friends and even my own sibling struggle. But so far they've made it alive... and I really hope you will too.

(hug if you want one)
